commits.pr_title: [Multimodal] Deprecate PyAV video decoder backend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose This PR deprecates and remove PyAV backend from video io for two reasons: 1. Poor performance: PyAV has a super poor performance comparing other CPU backend like OpenCV/Torchcodec, because it only provides seek api which is inefficient for frames sampling. Even if with sparse sampling optimization, it still only wins OpenCV in super sparse case which is quite rare (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44598#issue-4593570914) 2. PyAV is an optional dependency in `vllm[audio]` with GNU license issue in its bundled ffmpeg, while Torchcodec has been added to commom deps and work out of box. Therefore, I don't see too much reasons for maintaining an optional video backend with poor performance and license issue. In the follow up PRs, we will try to migrate audio IO to `torchcodec` and `torchaudio`, so that we can enable audio support by default (see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51826) (Thanks @JaredforReal for helping benchmarking each video backend!) ## Test Plan ## Test Result ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Capture the widest uniform decode batch by default
commits.pr_body:
# [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Capture the widest uniform decode batch by default

## Purpose

This PR was four fixes; at a maintainer's request it is now one. The others are
#50531 (warmup lookahead reservation) and #50532 (uniform-decode dispatch). The
rejection-sampler argmax fix is dropped from this stack in favour of #50183,
which covers the same defect.

`max_cudagraph_capture_size` defaults in units of *tokens*
(`min(max_num_seqs * 2, 512)`) while the batch it has to cover is
`max_num_seqs * (1 + num_speculative_tokens)` tokens. With speculation on, the
widest uniform decode batch falls outside the captured range and the largest
decode steps dispatch eager. On a lane at `max_num_seqs=32` and
`num_speculative_tokens=16` the decode capture list collapses to a single entry
while the log still reads `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, which is why the correct value had
to be found by hand and passed as `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 544` during
bring-up. 544 is exactly `32 * (1 + 16)`, and the rule here derives it.

The fix keeps the historical ceiling for the token-strided grid and adds the
decode sizes as a *request-count* grid scaled by query length, capped at 512
requests. Sizing the token grid off the speculative width instead would multiply
the number of captured graphs; that was the first shape of this fix and it is
not what is proposed here.

Two properties the tests pin:

- Without speculation the default is bit-identical to the historical
  `min(max_num_seqs * 2, 512)` for every `max_num_seqs` from 8 to 2048, so no
  non-speculative configuration changes.
- Under a dynamic speculative schedule the draft width varies per batch size, so
  capture sizes are generated per tier rather than for the widest width alone.
  Covering only the widest leaves the narrower tiers dispatching eager.

This is a `VllmConfig` default rather than a runner-specific path, so it affects
V1 as well as V2.

## Test Plan

`tests/compile/test_config.py` asserts the rule directly rather than through an
engine: the non-speculative equivalence sweep above, that the widest uniform
decode batch lands inside the captured range once speculation is on, that the
cap is applied to requests rather than tokens, and that every tier of a dynamic
schedule is covered.

## Test Result

`pytest tests/compile/test_config.py` on an H100 sandbox, this branch overlaid
on the pinned nightly wheel (`0.26.1rc1.dev77+g6f91edf96`): **53 passed, 9
failed**.

The 9 failures are environmental and pre-existing — the same 9 fail on the
unmodified tree in the same container, all with `ValueError: Free memory on
device`, because the box had 75 GiB of 81 GiB of GPU memory held by another
process. They are the engine-launching tests (`test_use_cudagraphs`,
`test_enforce_eager`, `test_no_compilation` and similar), none of which is a
capture-size test. Against that same baseline this branch takes the pass count
from 33 to 53.

Revert check: restoring the pre-existing formula fails exactly the
`covers_widest_uniform_decode` cases — including the off-stride case, where the
scalar ceiling coincidentally matches but the widest batch is still absent from
`cudagraph_capture_sizes` — plus `caps_requests_not_tokens`, while leaving all
16 `unchanged_without_speculation` cases passing.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on every touched file.

### Model evaluation

`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 400 questions, 5-shot, greedy, on
`Qwen/Qwen3-4B` with the published `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16` drafter at
`num_speculative_tokens=16`, V2 model runner, single H100: **accuracy 0.880,
0.000 invalid, 400 questions**. This was measured on the combined set of fixes
before the split, so it covers this change together with the others rather than
in isolation.

## Related

- #30330 — the earlier fix to the same capture-size default that this completes.
- #46324 aligns spec-decode capture sizes for PIECEWISE mode specifically and
  does not touch the default ceiling; #49390 raises the Blackwell capture
  default as a platform tuning choice rather than fixing the unit mismatch.

I checked for duplicate and overlapping open PRs (`gh pr list --search` on
"cudagraph capture size speculative", "max_cudagraph_capture_size",
"uniform decode capture").

I used AI assistance (Cursor) to draft, test, and validate this change, and I
reviewed every changed line before submitting.

- `scatter_kv_caches` `token_indices_tensor`
- `gather_kv_caches` `token_indices_tensor`

Same class of stall #53491 adds a stricter check for: `torch.tensor(list, device="cpu")` without `pin_memory=True` yields a pageable CPU tensor, and the subsequent `.to(device, non_blocking=True)` is silently staged by the CUDA driver and blocks the host. Follows the same pattern as #54266 (Qwen VL rotary position IDs) and #54292 (three MM encoder paths); this PR covers the two hf3fs scatter/gather sites, which are on the KV connector data-path.

commits.pr_title: [Test] Assert co-located RayExecutorV2 stores publish distinct ports
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up requested by @AndreasKaratzas when merging #50969 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50969#issuecomment-5457958170): that PR removed `test_colocated_tcpstore_ports_differ` together with the `_select_tcpstore_port` formula it patched, but the invariant that test guarded is externally meaningful and should keep coverage on the new path.

Invariant: replicas sharing a host must never publish the same rank-0 TCPStore port. With `create_dist_init_method()` each rank-0 actor binds a kernel-assigned ephemeral port and holds the store for its lifetime, so concurrently live replicas cannot collide.

## Changes

`tests/distributed/test_ray_v2_executor.py`:

- Add `test_colocated_dist_init_stores_hold_distinct_ports`: three detached rank-0 `RayWorkerProc`s call `create_dist_init_method()`; asserts the published ports are pairwise distinct, each equals the port its own store actually bound, none is a privileged port, and all are still held (a contender `bind` gets `EADDRINUSE`) while the replicas are alive.
- Factor the detached-worker construction and the held-port check into `_detached_rank0_worker()` / `_assert_port_held()` shared with the existing `test_dist_init_store_owns_port`; that test's assertions are unchanged.

Effectiveness check: pinning `TCPStore(port=...)` to a fixed value makes the new test fail with `len({29517}) == 1 != 3` — torch's `multi_tenant` store silently reuses the in-process server, so a regression to a fixed or derived port would publish one port for every replica, which is exactly the collision the original regression test was written for.

## Test Plan

Run inside the `vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image (2026-08-20, aarch64/GB200):

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_ray_v2_executor.py -k dist_init_store -v
```

## Test Result

- `test_dist_init_store_owns_port` PASSED, `test_colocated_dist_init_stores_hold_distinct_ports` PASSED (2 passed in 13.6s).
- Mutation run with the store pinned to a fixed port: the new test FAILED as intended.
- Full file `pytest tests/distributed/test_ray_v2_executor.py -v` on 4 GPUs in the same image: 23 passed in 9m34s.
- `pre-commit run --files tests/distributed/test_ray_v2_executor.py`: all hooks passed.

## Notes

- Not a duplicate: no open PR touches this test file or the colocated-port coverage (`gh pr list --search "colocated tcpstore"` / `"50969 in:body"`).
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the change was reviewed line by line and the tests above were run by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Release model and KV cache on in-process engine shutdown
commits.pr_body:
With `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0` the engine shares the caller's process,
so teardown has to actually drop its references — process exit does not cover
for it. Two module-level holders keep the top-level model alive past
`GPUModelRunner.shutdown()`, and because the model owns the layers that alias
the KV allocation, the KV cache stays resident with it.

Surfaced by AMD CI as
`tests/v1/e2e/test_hybrid_chunked_prefill.py::test_qwen_mtp_mamba_prefix_cache_hit_is_bounded`:
```
ValueError: Memory of devices devices=[0, 1, 2, 3] not free after dur_s=240.29
```

The test **body passed** — all three generation waves completed. Only the
post-test memory check failed, with device 0 holding 24.11 GiB across 241
bit-identical polls over 240 s. Bit-identical rules out lazy ROCm reclamation,
which decays.

Shutdown *is* reached, so this is not a missed teardown call:
`UniProcExecutor.shutdown` → `WorkerWrapperBase.shutdown` → `GPUWorker.shutdown`
→ `model_runner.shutdown()` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:1448`).

### Holder 1 — `_language_model_by_module`

A module-level `dict[nn.Module, VllmModel]` in
`vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py`, keyed on the **top-level model** by
identity with a strong reference, and never cleared — five references in the
production tree before this PR: one definition, one `in`, one read, two writes. It is a GC root, so
`gc.collect()` can never reclaim what it keys on.

It is populated in this configuration: the MTP path calls
`target_model.get_language_model()` at
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py:56`, and
`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` does not override it.

Fix: make it a `WeakKeyDictionary`. The cached value is a submodule of the key
and torch modules hold no parent back-reference, so the value cannot resurrect
the key.

### Holder 2 — `LLMEngine._finalizer`

`vllm/v1/engine/llm_engine.py:131` (pre-patch) passes the model as a
`weakref.finalize` argument. CPython's `finalize` stores its args strongly in a
class-level registry until the finalizer fires, and it fires only once the
`LLMEngine` is collected — which has not happened while the caller still holds
the handle.

Fix: pass a weak reference and no-op if it is dead.

The hook being removed is registered as a **bound method** of the wrapper module
(`vllm/compilation/wrapper.py:157-158`), so dynamo's registry keeps the *wrapper*
alive independently. That does not by itself imply the top-level model is alive:
the wrapper is a submodule, and torch modules hold no parent back-reference, so
in principle a wrapper could outlive the model and its hook would then go
uncleaned. I have not found a case where that happens, and the alternative is
pinning ~9 GiB of VRAM for the life of the engine — but this trade-off wants a
reviewer's judgement rather than my assurance.

**Both must land together.** Either holder alone keeps the model alive, so
fixing one frees nothing. That is measured, not assumed — see Test Result.

### Why this surfaced now

`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` is `is_hybrid`, so it ran Model Runner V1
until #53183 removed the `is_hybrid` gate from the default-runner selection.
Both holders predate the #53183 default flip and affect MRV1 equally — MRV1
reaches the same cache via `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py:1414`.
(They postdate MRV2 itself, which landed in #25266.) MRV1 simply stayed under
this test's memory budget, because it *additionally* severs each layer's alias
of the KV allocation in `_cleanup_profiling_kv_cache`
(`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:6656`), which MRV2 does not.

So the runner flip did not create these holders; it removed the slack that was
hiding them.

### Relationship to PR #41594

[#41594](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41594) proposed porting MRV1's
KV sever into MRV2's `free_before_shutdown`, and was closed unmerged with:

> clearing `compilation_config.static_forward_context` and doing `del` on the
> model should make the tensors eligible for GC/free.

**That review was correct, and this PR is the missing half of it.** `del` on the
model does free the KV — provided the model can actually die. The two holders
above are why it could not. With them fixed, the reviewer's premise holds and no
sever is needed. The measurements below confirm this directly, and are why the
sever is *not* part of this PR (see "Considered and dropped").

### Not a duplicate

**#54246 is concurrent work in the same area and is complementary, not
competing.** [#54246](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54246)
("[Bugfix][MRV2] Release layer-bound KV cache memory in shutdown()", opened
2026-08-28) does the per-layer KV sever that this PR deliberately drops. The two
fix different holders:

| | frees | leaves held |
|---|---|---|
| #54246 (sever the layer→KV aliases) | the 12.0 GiB KV cache | the 8.9 GiB of weights |
| this PR (unpin the model) | both, since `del self.model` then drops the layers | — |

Measured, same box and config (full table below): sever-only lands at
**10.46 GiB**, unpin-only at **2.99 GiB**. So #54246 alone does not close the
failure that motivated either PR, and this PR alone does. They are still worth
having together — #54246 restores MRV1/MRV2 parity and protects the case where
something else pins the model — and I would rather rebase onto it than duplicate
it.

**Overlap to resolve:** both PRs change `tests/conftest.py` in the same place
(replacing the silent `except Exception: pass` in `VllmRunner.__exit__` with a
log). Whichever lands second should drop its copy; happy for that to be mine.

Other prior art reviewed: #41594 (closed, above); #42074 (closed, MRV1 offloader
singleton — same family of module-level holder, different object); #46023 (open,
`LLMEngine`/`EngineCore` field retention — adjacent, does not cover either
holder here); #51024 (open, test-only diagnostic that would have named the
holder had it been merged). None fixes the two holders here.

## Test Plan

### GPU

Reproduce the failing configuration and measure what teardown actually releases.
Model Qwen3.5-4B (hybrid GDN + MTP), `tensor_parallel_size=1`,
`max_model_len=8192`, `kv_cache_memory_bytes=12 GiB`, `enforce_eager=True`,
`enable_chunked_prefill=True`, `enable_prefix_caching=True`,
`mamba_cache_mode="align"`, `speculative_config={"method": "mtp",
"num_speculative_tokens": 2}`, `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`.

Measured quantity: VRAM in use on device 0 after
`engine_core.shutdown(timeout=60)` → `del llm` → `torch._dynamo.reset()` →
`gc.collect()` → `empty_cache()` → `synchronize()`, i.e. precisely the sequence
`VllmRunner.__exit__` performs before the memory check that failed in CI.

Four arms, each from a clean device: Model Runner V1; MRV2 unpatched; MRV2 with
only MRV1's KV sever added; MRV2 with only this PR.

Plus an over-free check: construct a second engine in the same process after the
first has shut down, and compare its output to the first.

### CPU

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_language_model_cache_is_weak.py \
       tests/v1/engine/test_llm_engine_finalizer_is_weak.py -v
```

One suite per holder. `test_language_model_cache_is_weak` asserts the cache is
weak-keyed and that a cached entry does not pin its key.
`test_llm_engine_finalizer_is_weak` documents that `weakref.finalize` holds args
strongly (the premise for holder 2), and asserts `_cleanup_instance_caches`
no-ops on a dead reference while still walking a live model.

Regression check — the only other suite touching `get_language_model`:

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni_embed.py
```

## Test Result

### GPU — VRAM retained on device 0 after shutdown

Run on MI355X. Device baseline before any engine: 0.62 GiB.

| Arm | Retained |
|---|---|
| Model Runner V1 (this arch's default before #53183) | 10.21 GiB |
| Model Runner V2, unpatched | **22.46 GiB** |
| Model Runner V2 + KV sever only | 10.46 GiB |
| Model Runner V2 + **this PR** | **2.99 GiB** |

The reproduction tracks the CI run: `Model loading took 8.91 GiB`,
`GPU KV cache size: 187,830 tokens`. The MRV1→MRV2 delta of 12.25 GiB is the KV
cache. Generated text was byte-identical across all four arms.

Row 3 is the load-bearing measurement. Severing the KV *without* unpinning the
model still leaks 10.46 GiB — the weights. Unpinning *without* severing reaches
2.99 GiB, because `del self.model` inside `shutdown()` then drops the layers
that alias the KV. The residual ~3 GiB is HIP context and library footprint.

### GPU — over-free check

Second engine constructed in the same process after the first shut down, with
only the two changes in this PR applied:

```
engine-1  live 26.52 GiB  ->  after shutdown 3.61 GiB
engine-2  live 26.75 GiB  ->  after shutdown 3.62 GiB
outputs identical; no accumulation across cycles
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][V1] Keep an encoder cache entry until its last occurrence is freed
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`EncoderCacheManager.cached` maps `mm_hash -> set[request_id]`. It counts referencing *requests*, not referencing *positions*, so a request that uses the same multi-modal item more than once holds exactly one reference covering every occurrence — `check_and_update_cache` for the second occurrence hits `cached[mm_hash].add(request_id)`, which is a no-op on a set that already contains it.

`free_encoder_input` then dropped that single reference as soon as the **first** occurrence was freed:

```python
self.cached[mm_hash].discard(req_id)
if not self.cached[mm_hash]:
    self.freeable[mm_hash] = num_encoder_embeds
    self.num_freeable_slots += num_encoder_embeds
```

so the entry became reclaimable capacity while the request still had later occurrences to splice in. The scheduler frees each input id independently as its token span is consumed (`_free_encoder_inputs` in `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`), so this is the ordinary path rather than an edge case. Once the entry is in `freeable`, any other request's `can_allocate` can evict it, `get_freed_mm_hashes` tells the workers to drop the tensor, and when the later occurrence reaches the encoder window `check_and_update_cache` misses and the encoder recomputes an item it had already computed.

The common trigger is an ordinary multi-turn vision conversation: the chat template inlines the same image once per turn, so a single request carries N features sharing one `mm_hash`, and every occurrence after the first can force a redundant encoder pass.

This is wasted encoder compute and cache thrash, not wrong output — the recompute path itself is correct, just unnecessary.

## Approach

Hold the request's reference until it has no cached input id left that maps to the same hash. The check runs over the request's own remaining cached ids, which is a handful of entries, and only on the free path.

`free()` still fully releases the entry, because it frees every cached input id and the last one finds no remaining occurrence.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py -v
```

Two new tests:

- `test_duplicate_mm_hash_stays_referenced_until_last_free` — freeing the first of two occurrences leaves the reference and `num_freeable_slots` untouched; freeing the second releases both.
- `test_duplicate_mm_hash_is_not_evicted_before_last_use` — with the entry still needed, a competing request cannot claim it as reclaimable capacity, the later occurrence still hits cache, and nothing is reported to the workers as freed.

The existing `test_free_request_with_duplicate_mm_hashes`, `test_basic_allocate_and_reuse` and `test_free_request_frees_all_inputs` are unchanged and still pass.

commits.pr_title: [Attention][DCP] Enable FlashInfer MLA for DSpark drafting
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

- Recompute rank-local DCP sequence lengths from the draft model's current global sequence lengths before every shared draft metadata build.
- Share that metadata plumbing across EAGLE, MTP, DFlash, and DSpark, removing DFlash's duplicate preparation.
- Keep causal target MLA layers and non-causal DSpark draft layers in separate KV-cache groups by requiring the group to agree on `non_causal_multi_token_decode`.
- Advertise FlashInfer MLA support for non-causal multi-token DCP drafting.
- Repeat global causal sequence boundaries when non-causal DSpark blocks are flattened into single-token decode rows.
- Add focused metadata and backend regressions.

## Motivation

DSpark needs two complementary pieces for FlashInfer MLA under DCP:

1. Draft attention must recompute rank-local sequence lengths from its own current global sequence lengths. Reusing target-local lengths is not sufficient because draft steps advance or rewind `input_buffers.seq_lens` after sampling and rejection.
2. FlashInfer's non-causal DSpark path flattens each query block into independent decode rows. Under DCP, the local block table and sequence lengths were expanded, but the global causal boundaries were not, leaving the native CP kernel with mismatched batch geometry.

The cache-group merge also used `any(non_causal_multi_token_decode)`, which could promote a causal target group to the draft's non-causal behavior. Requiring agreement keeps target and draft groups distinct.

Putting rank-local preparation in the shared draft metadata builder also fixes the same missing plumbing for EAGLE and MTP while preserving existing DFlash behavior.

## Tests

Passed:

- 12 focused B300 unit tests covering FlashInfer MLA DCP metadata/backend behavior
- pre-commit/static validation before the conflict-free rebase
- `uvx --offline ruff check` on all eight changed Python files after combining the commits
- `uvx --offline ruff format --check`
- `python3 -m py_compile`
- `git diff --check`

End-to-end Kimi-K3 DSpark+DCP evaluation is pending because the available dev GPUs were occupied.

## Relationship to existing work

- Builds on causal native FlashInfer MLA DCP support from #54012.
- Independent of the scheduler/verifier/full-CUDA-graph fixes in #54102.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used to compare k3-dev with current upstream, trace the shared draft metadata paths, isolate the backend-independent and FlashInfer-specific pieces, write the initial patches/tests, and run validation. The submitter will review every changed line and complete end-to-end evaluation.

commits.pr_title: [Hy4] support Hy4-preview model
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

# Hy4 preview Usage Guide

  Hy4 preview is Tencent Hy's new-generation open-source Mixture-of-Experts language
  model. Its backbone has 770B total parameters with 49B activated per token across
  78 layers. The first layer uses a dense FFN; the other 77 layers use 256 routed
  experts (top-8) and 1 shared expert. A native MTP layer adds 10B total parameters
  (0.7B activated) for speculative decoding.

  On the architecture side, inspired by DeepSeek and GLM, the attention module employs Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention (Gated DSA) with IndexCache for cross-layer sparse index reuse. The residual pathway uses iHC (identity Hyper-Connections) to expand inter-layer information flow.

  ## vLLM Setup

  Choose one of the following setup methods.

  ### Using Docker

  ```bash
  docker run --gpus all \
    -p 8000:8000 \
    --ipc=host \
    -e VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1 \
    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
    vllm/vllm-openai:hy4-preview tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
      --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
      --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
      --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
      --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
      --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
      --enable-auto-tool-choice \
      --port 8000 \
      --served-model-name hy4-preview
  ```

  Build vLLM from source:

  ```bash
  uv venv --python 3.12 --seed --managed-python
  source .venv/bin/activate
  git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git
  cd vllm
  uv pip install --editable . --torch-backend=auto
  ```

  ## vLLM Deployment

  Start the FP8 model with MTP enabled:

  ```bash
  export VLLM_ENABLE_HPC_OPS=1

  vllm serve tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"mtp"}' \
    --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE \
    --tool-call-parser hy_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --port 8000 \
    --served-model-name hy4-preview
  ```

  ## OpenAI Client Example

  Tencent recommends `temperature=0.9` and `top_p=1.0`. Reasoning defaults to
  `high`, which is suitable for math, coding, and other complex tasks.

  ```python
  from openai import OpenAI

  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")

  response = client.chat.completions.create(
      model="hy4-preview",
      messages=[
          {"role": "user", "content": "Hello! Can you briefly introduce yourself?"},
      ],
      temperature=0.9,
      top_p=1.0,
  )
  output_msg = response.choices[0].message
  print(output_msg.reasoning_content)  # chain-of-thought
  print(output_msg.content)             # final answer
  ```

  For a direct response without deep reasoning, pass `reasoning_effort="no_think"`:

  ```python
  response = client.chat.completions.create(
      model="hy4-preview",
      messages=[
          {"role": "user", "content": "Hello! Can you briefly introduce yourself?"},
      ],
      temperature=0.9,
      top_p=1.0,
      extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"reasoning_effort": "no_think"}},
  )
  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
  ```

  ### cURL Usage

  ```bash
  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{
      "model": "hy4-preview",
      "messages": [
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Hello! Can you briefly introduce yourself?"}
      ],
      "temperature": 0.9,
      "top_p": 1.0
    }'
  ```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][AMD] Annotate draft KV cache groups on the hybrid grouping path
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose Serving **Kimi-K3** (`KimiLinearForCausalLM` — 93 layers: 24 full-attention MLA + 69 KDA linear-attention) with the **DSpark MTP draft** (`Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`) and a CPU KV offload tier, the external prefix cache never serves anything: `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` stays pinned at exactly 0 for the life of the server while `vllm:kv_offload_store_bytes_total` grows without bound. The offload tier writes continuously and reads back nothing. The same latent defect affects any hybrid (attention + Mamba) model with an EAGLE-family drafter that reaches the general multi-group KV-cache grouping path. ## Root cause `is_eagle_group` is set in exactly one place in the tree: `_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`). It is gated on `model_version == "deepseek_v4"` and is reachable only from the `group_and_unify_kv_cache_specs` branch of `get_kv_cache_groups`. Kimi-K3 is MLA + Mamba, so it lands on the general multi-group path and **no group is annotated at all**. Consumers respond to "no group annotated" by flagging *every* group as a draft group — both `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` and the `OffloadingConnector` scheduler (`offloading/scheduler.py`, `eagle_groups = set(range(len(kv_cache_groups)))`). That fallback is documented as conservative, and it is — for full-attention groups. For a **Mamba** group it is not: 1. `get_sliding_window_size_in_chunks` returns `1` for a `MambaSpec` — "Mamba depends on a single state". 2. The eagle flag then applies `required_window += 1` → **2**. 3. `_sliding_window_lookup` reports a hit only on `consecutive_hits == sliding_window_size`, i.e. **two adjacent stored chunks**. 4. Under `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, exactly one state checkpoint is materialized per scheduler step; the chunks in between are null blocks (`block_id == 0`) and are skipped on store. 5. Two adjacent mamba chunks are therefore **never both stored**, so the group can never report a hit. 6. `_lookup` takes the minimum across groups, so `num_hit_chunks == 0` zeroes the whole request. ## What this means concretely for Kimi-K3 + DSpark The Mamba page forces a **1536-token block**, and the draft's 5 MLA layers are the smallest spec bucket, so `group_size` collapses to 5 — giving **20 KV cache groups: 5 target-MLA, 14 Mamba, 1 draft**. (Consistent with the two page-padding warnings every DSpark run logs: `4.17% = 1/24` and `1.45% = 1/69`.) At `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` a KDA checkpoint lands every **21 chunks = 32,256 tokens**. | | Groups flagged | Mamba group lookup | Result | |---|---|---|---| | **before** | 20 / 20 | needs 2 adjacent chunks at a 21-chunk stride | unsatisfiable → `get_num_new_matched_tokens` returns 0 for every prompt-shaped request | | **after** | 1 / 20 (the draft) | window stays 1, satisfied by a single checkpoint | lookup is no longer structurally zeroed; the 5 target-MLA groups also stop taking the eagle last-chunk drop | The failure is silent today. A vetoed lookup is not counted as a *query* either, so the hit **rate** stays empty rather than visibly dropping — there is no counter an operator can watch go wrong. Hence the second half of this patch. ## The fix Annotate **by spec rather than by model version**. `non_causal_multi_token_decode` is set exactly on drafter attention layers (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/dspark_mla.py`), is declared on `MLAAttentionSpec` as "Marks draft groups that flatten a non-causal query block into decode rows", and is propagated through `MLAAttentionSpec.merge` via `any(...)`. So it identifies the draft group wherever grouping happens to land. Two functions, both called at the end of the general multi-group path: - `_annotate_eagle_groups_from_draft_spec` — flags groups whose merged spec carries the marker. - `_warn_if_unannotated_eagle_mamba` — warns when speculative decoding is on, no group could be identified, and Mamba groups are present. That combination still takes the flag-all path and should not fail silently. ## Why this is not a duplicate | PR | What it does | Why it does not cover this | |---|---|---| | **#47891** — Exclude DSpark draft KV-cache group from OffloadingConnector lookup poisoning | Adds `eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` so an *identified* draft group's miss does not veto the request | The flag is only ever set inside `_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4`. On an unannotated model the exempt set is empty and nothing changes. The PR says so explicitly: *"Left empty in the 'flag all groups' fallback below … we conservatively keep the original behavior."* Kimi-K3 is precisely that case. | | **#48459** — core-tier half of #47891 | Same mechanism on `HybridKVCacheCoordinator` | Same single DSV4-gated setter; same gap. | | **#48375** — Honor `drop_eagle_block` in `MambaManager` | Fixes silent recurrent-state corruption on the GPU tier | Different bug. Does not touch group annotation or the offload lookup window. | | **#41640** — Add `is_eagle` in `AttentionSpec` | Generic annotation infrastructure that would attack the same root | Open and untouched since May 2026. If it lands, this patch should be rebased onto it. | No open PR mentions `required_window` or `_sliding_window_lookup` at all. **This patch is the missing precondition for #47891/#48459 rather than a competitor.** It stops the flag-all fallback from firing; they stop the identified draft group from vetoing. They compose, and on a hybrid model neither is sufficient alone. ## Test plan E2E KK3 test Four tests added to `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: - `test_draft_group_annotated_on_hybrid_general_path` — on an MLA + Mamba + draft-MLA fixture, exactly one group is flagged, it is the draft's, and no Mamba group is flagged. - `test_draft_group_not_annotated_without_spec_decode` — the marker alone flags nothing. - `test_unidentifiable_draft_with_mamba_warns` — the warning fires when no draft can be identified. - `test_no_warning_when_draft_group_is_identified` — and stays quiet when one can. ## Test result Unit tests: ``` tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_mla_draft_prefers_standard_layout_when_pages_can_be_unified PASSED [ 16%] tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_draft_group_annotated_on_hybrid_general_path PASSED [ 33%] tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_mamba_groups_never_flagged_even_when_draft_shares_a_group PASSED [ 50%] tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_draft_group_not_annotated_without_spec_decode PASSED [ 66%] tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_unidentifiable_draft_with_mamba_warns PASSED [ 83%] tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_no_warning_when_draft_group_is_identified PASSED [100%] ``` E2E Kimik3: on E2E I've measured the following improvements with the PR Config: ISL 8192 / OSL 1024 / conc 16, 24 sessions, TP8, DSpark, 64 GiB offload pool, GPU KV capped to 163,840 tokens so the 221 k working set evicts. ## Accuracy / serving eval Kimi-K3 gsm8k accuracy with CPU offload + DSpark MTP ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Save exact Mamba boundary states
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Fix Mooncake Store persistence for Mamba `align` mode by saving the exact core-selected boundary-state blocks and keeping those physical blocks alive until every worker rank has finished the asynchronous store attempt.

This fixes a correctness bug that could persist null, stale/reassigned, or live speculative Mamba state under a valid prefix hash. A later external prefix hit could then restore poisoned recurrent state and produce garbled or runaway output.

## Root cause

Mooncake's normal save path resolved each group's source block positionally from a worker-side snapshot of the request's block IDs. That is valid for append-only attention block tables, but a Mamba `align` table is sparse and mutable:

- superseded state positions are replaced by the null block and their physical blocks are freed;
- speculative scratch blocks are relocated to different logical positions;
- the connector's block-ID mirror is append-only and does not observe those in-place changes.

Consequently, a positional Mamba save could interpret `NULL_BLOCK_ID` as a physical source, or read a block that had already been freed, reassigned, or was still speculative, while using the correct chained prefix hash as its key. Mooncake's `batch_is_exist` deduplication could then preserve the bad value and prevent a later correct save from replacing it.

The production symptom was exposed by the DSpark/EAGLE lookup path landing on an affected interior key. Without that path, a later valid CoW boundary key could win and mask the corruption.

## Design

- Core emits exact `(group_id, block_id, boundary_tokens)` entries for committed Mamba `align` boundary states, including the CoW target for a sub-block partial tail. The connector never reconstructs these source IDs positionally.
- Mooncake excludes Mamba groups from the normal positional `store_mask`; exact boundary handoffs are the only Mamba writer. The normal path also skips null or missing source IDs for every group as a defense-in-depth guard.
- The scheduler claims each accepted physical block with `BlockPool.touch()` before it can be recycled. Consumer-only roles are gated before claiming or queueing handoffs.
- Each claimed block receives a monotonic handoff ID. A one-ID/one-pin mapping makes reference release and the bounded in-flight capacity exact, even though a request-level batch ID could work while all entries in a request complete together.
- Workers report a cross-rank completion watermark. After seeing its first handoff, a rank reports watermark `0` while that handoff is pending rather than omitting metadata; this prevents aggregation from ignoring a lagging rank and releasing a block early. Dedup, successful upload, pressure drop, cancellation, and store failure are all terminal outcomes for lifetime purposes.
- The scheduler releases the connector-owned refs only through `BlockPool.free_blocks()` after the aggregated watermark says every rank is terminal. The configurable in-flight cap bounds pinned GPU blocks if acknowledgements stop; saves beyond the cap remain best-effort and are dropped.
- Resumed prefills use the tracked prefill/save boundary, not the request's original prompt length, so replayed generated tokens retain the same cross-group save coverage.
- Mamba speculative scratch relocation remains an in-table move, but now fails closed unless `BlockPool.is_block_writable()` confirms the block is non-null, exclusively owned (`ref_cnt == 1`), and unhashed. If shared or pinned speculative blocks become valid in the future, this path must use CoW instead of relocating them.

This implementation is intentionally limited to Mamba `align` mode. Mooncake Store's configuration validation rejects incompatible non-align/`all` Mamba layouts; this PR does not add `all`-mode support.

## Retention semantics

`VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL` remains effective even though Mooncake's positional `store_mask` is false for Mamba:

1. Core `MambaManager.cache_blocks()` applies the retention policy first.
2. Only retained/materialized states receive a block hash.
3. Handoff emission skips null or unhashed blocks.
4. Mooncake stores the exact retained states from those handoffs.

Therefore dense default retention, sparse interval checkpoints, and replay-boundary behavior are preserved. External persistence is still best-effort: an eligible checkpoint may be absent if the handoff cap is reached or the store operation fails.

## Scope and overlap

This is not duplicate work:

- #50359 validates external lookup boundaries.
- #46896 and #46906 concern Mamba all-mode support and retention policy.
- #51362 independently adds the same defensive null/missing-block check to Mooncake's normal save loop. That check is included here, but this PR also removes unsafe positional Mamba saving and fixes exact source selection, asynchronous lifetime, retention-aware handoff, partial-tail handling, and speculative ownership. In that sense, this PR subsumes #51362's behavior rather than relying on it.

## Validation

Focused Mooncake Store and prefix-cache suites were run through the final design, including exact block-ID handoff, dense and sparse retention, partial tails, resumed prefills, more than two Mamba groups, null/missing sources, consumer skip-save behavior, cross-rank watermarking, bounded pins, failure paths, and exclusive speculative ownership.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py
```

Result: 183 passed. Additional focused reruns after the watermark, save-gate, and ownership-invariant changes passed (195 tests), and a broader Mooncake Store + prefix-cache run in the k3-debug container on a GB300 worker passed (219 tests). Ruff and `git diff --check` also passed.

Serving/model evaluation on `k3-pd-mooncake aa-lcr`:

- post-fix: 0/200 garbled responses;
- `llm_judge`: approximately 0.77/0.76;
- external prefix hit rate: approximately 91–98%;
- pre-fix baseline: garbled/runaway outputs, with `llm_judge` approximately 0.76/0.78.

No model kernels or numerical computation were changed.

AI assistance was used. The human submitter reviewed the changes and is responsible for understanding, testing, and defending the final submission.

## Purpose

Part of #53343. Split from #53344.

Level-2 sleep discards weight-tagged allocations and reloads parameters. Plain model tensor attributes are neither checkpoint parameters nor discoverable through `named_buffers`, so their semantic values can be lost even though their virtual addresses remain stable.

## Changes

Register static runtime tensors as non-persistent model buffers for:

- Gemma3n runtime scales;
- Conformer relative positional encodings;
- Voxtral mel filters;
- ERNIE 4.5 VL visual-token tensor caches.

The buffers remain excluded from `state_dict` while participating in the existing level-2 sleep buffer save/restore path.

Adds an allocation-level level-2 reproducer and a parameterized end-to-end regression test covering every model changed by this PR through its real top-level model:

- FireRedASR2 for the shared Conformer encoder;
- Gemma3n;
- Voxtral;
- ERNIE 4.5 VL.

Each case runs `generate`, locates the target runtime tensors by model type and `getattr`, saves their values and addresses, saves the dummy model parameters, enters level-2 sleep, wakes the weight mappings normally, reloads the parameters, wakes the KV cache, and runs `generate` again. The snapshot helper deliberately does not use `named_buffers`, so the same test can run on both the pre-fix and post-fix branches.

The FireRedASR2 Hugging Face override is invoked more than once during config loading and can receive a generic `PreTrainedConfig` without the repository-specific `audio_encoder_conf` extension. The test now creates the complete minimal encoder configuration when that field is absent instead of unconditionally updating it.

No test-side memory poisoning is performed; the test exercises the real physical-page contents returned by the CUDA driver. It verifies immediately after weights wake-up that every target tensor keeps both its value and virtual address, then verifies that generated tokens and selected-token logprobs are unchanged.

OpenPangu and the Static Sink Attention issues exposed by its test have been moved to follow-up PR #53696.

## Dependency

Independent. Can merge directly into `main`. PR #53696 depends on this PR for the shared sleep-mode test framework.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q tests/model_executor/test_sleep_mode_tensor_ownership.py
pytest -q tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py -k level2_discards
```

Changed files pass Ruff, `git diff --check`, and Python compilation. The end-to-end cases require a supported Linux CUDA runtime; the configured remote CUDA development container was unavailable during this update. The local Python test environment is also missing the repository's `tblib` dependency, so executable pytest coverage is left to CI.

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector] Support MooncakeStore with hybrid DCP prefix caching
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR enables `MooncakeStoreConnector` for mamba hybrid models (e.g., kimi k3) using decode context parallelism (DCP) and fixes a bug where incorrect load keys are constructed under fine-grained prefix hits, causing KV load failures.

### Failure Example

Consider Kimi-K3 with DCP 8 + DSpark and `--prefix-match-unit 128`:

- **Attention block span under DCP:** 1,536 × 8 = 12,288 tokens
- **Mamba block span:** 1,536 tokens
- **Prefix-match unit:** 128 tokens

Reproduction steps:
1. Send a 15,000-token prompt.
2. Clear GPU local cache.
3. Send the same prompt again.

#### Cache blocks stored and keys:

| KV group | Stored state | Store-key hash |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full attention | First physical block through 12,288 | `H_12288` |
| Full attention | Second physical block valid through 14,848 | `H_14848` |
| Mamba | Checkpoint at 13,824 | `H_13824` |
| Mamba | Partial state at 14,848 | `H_14848` |

#### Lookup

1. Attention matches its second physical block under `H_14848`.
3. EAGLE rewinds one 128-token unit, reducing the candidate hit length to 14,720.
4. Mamba has no checkpoint at 14,720, so it falls back to `H_13824`.
5. All groups converge to a safe `hit_length = 13,824`.

The existing load path derives the key for a group's partially reused physical block from `hit_length`. As a result, it requested `H_13824` for the attention block, even though that physical block was stored under `H_14848`. Mooncake therefore returned `-704` because the derived key did not exist.

This PR fixes this load failure by recording the precise token boundaries for partial cache store so that subsequent load requests can use the correct load key.

## Test Plan
- Mooncake store unit tests
- E2E Kimi k3 accuracy with dspark and mooncake

## Test Result
- Validated Kimi k3 DCP + dspark produces coherent results with mooncake external cache hits by clearing GPU local cache.
- Validate the same workload which causes `-704` load failure now passes with the fix.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Take the raw buffer in mm tensor lowering when possible
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a performance bug in the Rust frontend's multimodal tensor lowering
(`rust/src/chat/src/multimodal/tensor.rs`).

`collect_tensors()` flattens the preprocessed encoder input with
`encoder_input.into_iter().collect()`. On dynamically-dimensioned arrays
(`ArrayD`), ndarray's `into_iter()` walks a slow per-element path: the
iterator must compute each element's address from the strides. Large
multimodal inputs spend far more time in this single lowering step than
in the rest of preprocessing, erasing the Rust frontend's latency
advantage for VLM serving.

When the array is in standard (row-major) layout the data is already
contiguous, so take the underlying buffer directly with
`into_raw_vec_and_offset()` (an ownership move, no traversal), handling
a possible offset between the allocation and the first element.
Non-standard layouts keep the existing per-element path, so behavior is
unchanged for strided views.

No behavior change: the wire bytes follow the array's logical row-major
order in both paths (asserted by a new unit test). Checked for duplicate
work: no open PR touches this path (searched `into_raw_vec`,
`ArrayD into_iter`, `mm tensor lowering rust`).

## Test plan

```
cd rust
cargo fmt -p vllm-chat -- --check
cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib multimodal::tensor
```

New unit test
`collect_tensors_lowering_matches_logical_order_for_both_layouts` builds
a standard-layout `Array2` and a non-standard-layout one
(`reversed_axes()`: same buffer, transposed strides) and asserts the
lowered wire bytes always equal the array's logical row-major iteration
order — covering both the fast path and the fallback path.

## Test results

- Unit tests: `7 passed; 0 failed` (including the new test)
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` clean

Benchmark (InternVL-1B OCR, 633 images, RTX 4090D, single image):

| Stage | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tensor lowering per image | 105ms | 2.85ms (**37x**) |
| Rust frontend e2e, c=10 cold cache, TTFT p50 | 0.28s* | 0.18s |

\* 0.28s is the Python frontend baseline on the same engine; the Rust
frontend without this fix is slower than Python because the lowering
overhead exceeds the preprocessing savings.

No output change: end-to-end OCR quality parity confirmed on the full
633-image set (mean label similarity within FP16/resize-kernel noise of
the Python frontend).

## Documentation

Not needed — internal performance fix, no API or behavioral change.

---

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code); the change was
reviewed, tested, and benchmarked end-to-end by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Gate cross-node MNNVL custom all-reduce by group capability
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52907.

A cross-node TP group on pre-Blackwell GPUs can enter
`torch.distributed._symmetric_memory.rendezvous()` during `CustomAllreduce`
construction even though the group cannot use MNNVL. The workers then block
before model-parallel initialization completes.

## Root cause

PR #50000 removed the previous blanket multi-node CustomAllreduce disable and
allowed supported world sizes, including TP=16, to attempt the MNNVL path. The
existing fallback happens only after the symmetric-memory rendezvous. On a
cross-node pre-Blackwell group, that rendezvous itself can block, so the
fallback is never reached.

## Change

Before allocating CustomAllreduce buffers or entering the MNNVL rendezvous:

- require a Blackwell-class CUDA device and PyTorch local multicast support;
- aggregate the local capability bit across the CPU process group with `MIN`,
  so every rank takes the same branch;
- return early and use the existing NCCL fallback when any rank is incapable.

Same-node CustomAllreduce behavior is unchanged. Multicast-capable Blackwell
process groups continue into the existing rendezvous, which remains the final
check that the group actually spans an MNNVL domain.

## Why this is not duplicate work

A live search for open PRs referencing #52907 and for the relevant cross-node
MNNVL / symmetric-memory rendezvous terms found no implementation of this fix.
Nearby work addresses different mechanisms:

- #48075 probes FlashInfer fused all-reduce on single-node bridged NVLink
  topologies;
- #53000 fixes Blackwell MNNVL Lamport mailbox publication and stage cleanup;
- #52778 reports a later cross-node GB200 CUDA-IPC failure after MNNVL
  initialization succeeds.

This PR is limited to preventing unsupported cross-node groups from entering
the `CustomAllreduce` MNNVL rendezvous in the first place.

## Validation

### Original failing topology: independent external A/B

The original reporter validated the production hunk on the exact deployment
class from #52907:

- DeepSeek-R1;
- TP=16 across two DGX H100 nodes;
- the same `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image digest in both arms;
- the same vLLM version in both arms:
  `0.26.1rc1.dev1133+gf94666b60`.

Results:

| Arm | Result |
|---|---|
| Unpatched control | Reproduced the exact 30-minute `Application timeout caused pair closure` failure |
| Same nightly with this PR's production hunk | Completed server initialization and all benchmark profiles successfully |

This is a clean matched A/B confirmation that the group-unanimity gate fixes
the reported H100 failure. The external run applied the production hunk to a
newer nightly rather than checking out this PR's exact commit, so it validates
the runtime change and its forward applicability; the test diff and branch
metadata remain covered separately below.

### Independent mechanism validation

Matched TP=16 controls used four nodes × four RTX 4090 GPUs, Ray executor,
`ib0`, a two-layer local Llama config, and `--load-format dummy`:

| Revision/configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| `6f00a1ae3bd4` known-good | PASS |
| `5f8f72866c49` first-known-bad | HANG |
| `5f8f72866c49` + `--disable-custom-all-reduce` | PASS |

During the bad run, sampled workers on all four nodes stopped in:

```text
torch.distributed._symmetric_memory.rendezvous
  -> CustomAllreduce._init_mnnvl_buffer
  -> CustomAllreduce.__init__
  -> init_model_parallel_group
```

Patched validation:

- focused unit tests: 6 passed, 4 deselected;
- cross-node TP=16 startup/stability: 3/3 PASS;
- every TP=16 run emitted the expected group fallback warning and did not enter
  `_symmetric_memory.rendezvous()` or `_init_mnnvl_buffer()`;
- same-node TP=4 control: PASS without the cross-node fallback warning;
- Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check`: passed;
- docs status: passed.

## CI status

The existing red `pre-commit` entries are authorization-gate failures: the
actual pre-commit job was skipped because this first-time-contributor PR does
not yet have a maintainer-provided `verified`, `ready`, or
`ready-run-all-tests` label. They are not lint or test failures.

## Evidence boundary

- The original 2×DGX H100 / DeepSeek-R1 / TP=16 runtime failure is now covered
  by a matched external control-versus-production-hunk A/B.
- The positive MNNVL-capable Blackwell path is intentionally unchanged and has
  not been runtime-validated here on GB200/GB300; admission is covered by the
  focused capability tests.
- Same-node behavior is unchanged and passed the TP=4 control.
- The external H100 run validates the production hunk on a newer nightly, not
  the exact PR commit or its test-only changes.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for investigation, validation orchestration, and patch
preparation. The human submitter reviewed every changed line, understands the
control flow and test assertions, and is responsible for the design and
reported results.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix ncclCommQueryProperties heap overflow with NCCL >= 2.31
commits.pr_body:
This PR is for fixing host heap corruption (flaky SIGSEGV) when running vLLM with NCCL >= 2.31, seen in multi-node expert-parallel serving (vLLM + DeepEP).

`ncclCommQueryProperties` fills the `ncclCommProperties` struct based on the version the caller declares in `props.version`. It never reads `props.size`. C callers get this right through `NCCL_COMM_PROPERTIES_INITIALIZER`, which declares the `NCCL_VERSION_CODE` of the headers the application was compiled against, i.e. the layout its buffer actually has. vLLM instead declared the runtime library version (`ncclGetRawVersion()`) while its ctypes struct only mirrored the NCCL 2.30 layout (56 bytes). NCCL 2.31 grew the struct to 144 bytes (`commHash`, `ginMinStride`, `ginConnectionType`, `ginSupport[64]`, `devCommRuntimeVersionSize`) behind a `props->version >= NCCL_VERSION(2, 31, 0)` gate, so with a 2.31 library vLLM passes the gate and NCCL writes 88 bytes past the end of the buffer. The corruption surfaces later as flaky SIGSEGV or glibc heap errors in unrelated code, once per worker process.

This PR extends the ctypes struct to the NCCL 2.31 layout as shipped in v2.31.2-1 (144 bytes, offsets verified against its `nccl_device/core.h`) and clamps the declared `props.version` to the version of the headers the layout was taken from (`NCCL_COMM_PROPERTIES_LAYOUT_VERSION = 23102`), matching the C initializer semantics. The clamp is what prevents this bug class from recurring: when a future NCCL adds fields behind a newer gate, the declared version will not pass that gate, so NCCL will not write fields the buffer does not have. Older NCCL libraries are unaffected because the declared version never exceeds the runtime version.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Add support for `truncate_prompt_tokens` and `truncation_side`
commits.pr_body:
Resolves #44280  truncate_prompt_tokens


Purpose

Basically, the Rust frontend was hard-rejecting these parameters before. If you tried to pass a really long prompt and told it to just keep the last 50 tokens, it would just throw an invalid request error. 

This fixes that by bringing it up to parity with how the Python side handles it. 

### What it does:
- Plumbs `truncate_prompt_tokens` (and the `truncation_side` flag) all the way down from the API request endpoints into the internal `TextRequest` struct.
- Hooks into `generate_inner` to actually slice the token array right after tokenization, but before it hits the engine.
- Supports the `-1` trick (where it automatically calculates how many tokens to drop based on the model's max context length minus the max output tokens).
- Added a safeguard for multimodal stuff (images): if truncation cuts off an image's token coordinates, it shifts the coordinates so the C++ engine doesn't segfault, or just drops the image entirely if it gets chopped off.

### Testing
Just run `cargo test -p vllm-server` and `cargo test -p vllm-text`. Everything passes locally. 

You can also test it live by starting the server with `VLLM_USE_RUST_API_SERVER=1` and curling the `/v1/completions` endpoint with `"truncate_prompt_tokens": 2`. If you check the token usage in the JSON response, it'll show it successfully dropped the rest of the prompt before processing.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Deflake the rms_norm scaling-property assertions
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

TestRMSNorm.test_native_semantics and TestFusedAddRMSNorm.test_native_semantics check that rms_norm(2x) == rms_norm(x), against inputs drawn from an unseeded torch.randn and a hard-coded atol=1e-3.

Two problems. The property is only approximate: epsilon does not scale with x, so rms_norm(2x) = x / sqrt(mean(x^2) + epsilon/4), which differs from rms_norm(x) by the epsilon term. And 1e-3 is tighter than the tolerance the op itself declares for float16 -- layernorm.py sets atol=1e-2, rtol=2e-3, with a comment explaining that the default float16 tolerance is too tight here.

Seed the generator, and compare with the op's declared tolerance via the assert_close helper already used elsewhere in this file, so there is one source of truth for it.

Measured on MI300-class hardware, running the assertion itself over 20000 RNG states for the float16 / epsilon=1e-5 case (the parametrization that failed in AMD CI -- note the test hard-codes 4x8 and ignores its n_tokens/hidden_size parameters, so every parametrization draws the same shape):

  max |rms_norm(2x) - rms_norm(x)|            0.00390625
  fails under hard-coded atol=1e-3/rtol=1e-3  9/20000  (0.045%)
  fails under op-declared atol=1e-2/rtol=2e-3 0/20000  (0%)

0.00390625 is 2 ULP of float16 in [2,4) and matches the value in the CI failure exactly. With ~30 float16 epsilon=1e-5 draws per run before this change, that is roughly a 1.3% chance of a spurious failure per CI run from this arm alone. Seed 0, now pinned, has a max deviation of 0.00012207.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Set breakable graph env before Ray actor import
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

DSv4 automatically enables breakable CUDA graphs in `VllmConfig`. Native
multiprocessing workers inherit that setting before importing the model, but
Ray creates its worker actors first and copies the driver environment only later
in `initialize_worker`.

That ordering matters because `@eager_break_during_capture` makes its decision
when the model module imports. Without the setting, the decorator permanently
returns the original attention and indexer functions. Ray later enables
breakable capture, but the breakpoints needed to keep those functions outside
the graph are missing, producing an oversized graph and garbled output.

Copy only `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` into the actor `runtime_env` before
import, for both Ray executors. All existing general environment propagation,
worker exclusions, and node-local values remain unchanged. This follows the
existing pre-actor environment pattern used for Ray device visibility in
#33308.

No open PR duplicates this Ray import-order fix; #41834 concerns unrelated
SM12x model support. AI assistance was used to investigate and prepare this
patch; I reviewed every changed line and the reported test results.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_ray_env_utils.py -q
```

physical GB300 hosts. Retain production CUDA graphs, expert parallelism, MNNVL,
and custom collectives, and do not explicitly set
`VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` so the test exercises automatic enablement.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Keep the Moondream3 MoE all-reduce out of the fused-path try
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`Moondream3TextMoE.forward` wrapped **both** the fused expert kernel and the
tensor-parallel all-reduce that follows it in a single `try/except
(NotImplementedError, RuntimeError)`:

```python
try:
    out = fused_experts(...)
    out = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(out)   # <-- inside the try
    return out
except (NotImplementedError, RuntimeError) as exc:
    self._use_fused_moe = False
    ...
# fallback Python expert loop
out = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(out)       # <-- all-reduces again
```

A `RuntimeError` raised by the **collective itself** was therefore caught and
treated as a fused-kernel failure. That rank disabled the fused path, ran the
Python expert loop, and issued a *second* all-reduce, while every peer issued
one. The tensor-parallel group desyncs and wedges permanently: all ranks stay
alive, no traceback is produced, and the job only ends when a test or step
timeout fires.

Note the failure is specific to the collective raising. If `fused_experts`
itself raises, both the old and new code all-reduce exactly once — that path
was never broken, which is why this went unnoticed.

This is a latent bug in the model, not a regression from any recent PR. It
became reachable on ROCm when #53183 ("[Model Runner V2] Use MRV2 for all
models by default") removed the `is_moe` gate from
`_is_default_v2_model_runner_model()`. `Moondream3ForCausalLM` declares
`moe_num_experts = 64`, is absent from the old
`DEFAULT_V2_MODEL_RUNNER_ARCHITECTURES` allowlist, and is not in
`ROCM_DEFAULT_MRV1_ARCHITECTURES`, so it moved from MRV1 to MRV2 on ROCm.

### Fix

Narrow the `try` to the expert computation and all-reduce exactly once at the
end of `forward`, on every path. The fallback loop moves into `_expert_loop`,
which returns this rank's partial output and does not communicate. A failing
collective now propagates instead of being retried.

## Test Plan

New CPU-only unit tests in
`tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3_moe.py`, marked
`pytest.mark.cpu_test`, running under a single-rank gloo TP group. They pin the
invariant that makes the bug impossible: **exactly one all-reduce per forward,
on every path.**

- `test_expert_loop_all_reduces_once` — Python fallback path
- `test_fused_path_all_reduces_once` — fused kernel path
- `test_all_reduce_failure_is_not_retried` — **the regression guard**: a
  collective that raises must propagate, not trigger a second collective
- `test_fallback_after_fused_failure_all_reduces_once[RuntimeError,
  NotImplementedError]` — fused failure still all-reduces once, and so does the
  next forward once the fused path is disabled

The router is stubbed so the test does not depend on platform-specific
`ReplicatedLinear` weight post-processing.

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_moondream3_moe.py -v
```

commits.pr_title: [Core][KV Connector] Start async KV loads after the forward launch when no sync loads are scheduled
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

In scaled P/D setups, decode workers spend significant host time posting NIXL pull requests: e.g. ~5 ms for 9 remote KV requests fanned out across TP8 (= 72 NIXL handles), with occasional spikes to ~48 ms. The expensive part is synchronous descriptor construction (`make_prepped_xfer()` + `transfer()`), which used to run in `pre_forward()` and therefore delayed the GPU model forward.

This PR defers `start_load_kv()` until **after** the current step's forward has been launched whenever the step has no synchronous KV loads, so the host-side load submission overlaps with GPU compute. It trades a negligible TTFT increase for a shorter TPOT.

### How it works

- The scheduler already knows per request whether its connector load is synchronous (`load_async=False`, i.e. the KV is consumed by the current step) or asynchronous. It now aggregates this into a new `SchedulerOutput.has_sync_kv_loads` flag (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`, `vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py`).
- On the worker side, both connector call sites honor the flag:
  - `ActiveKVConnector` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/kv_connector.py`): `pre_forward()` calls `start_load_kv()` immediately only when `has_sync_kv_loads` is set; otherwise it marks the load start pending and `post_forward()` runs it after the forward launch. The `no_forward` path still starts any deferred load exactly once.
  - `KVConnectorModelRunnerMixin._get_kv_connector_output()` (`vllm/v1/worker/kv_connector_model_runner_mixin.py`): same ordering — sync loads run before the yield, async loads run in the `finally` after the forward launch, still ordered after any in-flight KV block zeroing.
- No config opt-in: the behavior is automatic. Steps that schedule a synchronous load keep the existing pre-forward ordering; steps with only async loads (or a mix — mixed steps conservatively keep the pre-forward path) benefit from the overlap.

### Connector rework

Because `start_load_kv()` / `wait_for_save()` now reliably run after the forward launch, connectors no longer need the `get_finished()` workaround to get compute/I-O overlap:

- **Mooncake store connector** (`mooncake/store/connector.py`, `mooncake/store/worker.py`): load and store submission moved out of `get_finished()` into real `start_load_kv()` and `wait_for_save()` implementations; `get_finished()` now only reports completed send/recv request IDs.
- **Simple CPU offload connector** (`simple_cpu_offload_connector.py`, `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py`): same move — loads are launched in `start_load_kv()`, stores in `wait_for_save()` (still gated on a compute-done event for the GPU→CPU direction, see #45704 / #39306); `get_finished()` only tracks completed transfer events.
- **LMCache connector** (`lmcache_connector.py`, `lmcache_integration/vllm_v1_adapter.py`): the per-step layerwise state (`current_layer`, `layerwise_retrievers`) was reset in `start_load_kv()`, but the layerwise hooks fire during every forward once metadata is bound — including before a deferred load start. The reset moves to a new `bind_connector_metadata()` hook, with a compat fallback for LMCache engines that predate the hook.
- `KVConnectorBase.start_load_kv()` docstring updated to document the new ordering contract (`kv_connector/v1/base.py`).

### Duplicate-work check

The closest open work is #45211, which offloads NIXL READ submission to a dedicated reader thread and introduces cross-thread queue/locking ownership. This PR is materially different and smaller: it creates no thread and no concurrent connector-state access; posting remains synchronous on the model-runner thread but occurs after the current model forward is enqueued. Searches for deferred `start_load_kv()` / `post_forward()` ordering found no equivalent open PR.

AI assistance was used for trace analysis, implementation support, tests, and preparation of this draft. The author will review the exact public diff before marking it ready for review.

## Test Plan

New/updated unit tests:

- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_has_sync_kv_loads` — covers async-only, sync-only, and mixed steps.
- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kv_connector.py` (new) — asserts `pre_forward` / `post_forward` / `no_forward` ordering of `start_load_kv` vs `wait_for_save` for both values of `has_sync_kv_loads`.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py` — updated to assert async loads start after the layer hooks rather than assuming the old pre-forward order.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py`, `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py` — updated for the `start_load_kv` / `wait_for_save` split (stores still gated on the compute-done event, loads are not).
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_simple_cpu_offload.py` — asserts a remote-prefill (async) load step reports `has_sync_kv_loads == False`.

End-to-end: two-node P/D setup with Qwen3-0.6B, one TP1 producer and one TP1 decoder, 1,319 GSM8K prompts at concurrency 64:

| Metric | Control A2 | Deferred B | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TTFT | 14,471.9 ms | 14,481.5 ms | +9.6 ms (+0.07%) |
| TPOT | 4.940 ms/token | 4.697 ms/token | -0.243 ms (-4.92%) |
| ITL | 4.939 ms/token | 4.701 ms/token | -0.239 ms (-4.83%) |
| E2E | 15,077.9 ms | 15,053.3 ms | -24.6 ms (-0.16%) |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Release layer-bound KV cache memory in shutdown()
commits.pr_body:
MRV2's `shutdown()` dropped the runner's own references but left the per-layer kv_cache bindings installed by `bind_kv_cache()` untouched. Since the model object can outlive the runner (e.g. `LLMEngine`'s finalizer holds it until engine deletion), the entire KV cache footprint stayed pinned for in-process engines until process exit.

Scrub the bindings on the main and draft models via a shared `clear_layer_kv_caches()` helper in vllm/v1/worker/utils.py, also reused by `_teardown_profiling_state()`. Also log engine-core shutdown failures in tests/conftest.py instead of silently swallowing them.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Pre-allocate `wvSplitKrc` static workspaces before KV init
commits.pr_body:
`wvSplitKrc`'s process-lifetime static workspaces (csrc/rocm/ skinny_gemms.cu) are allocated lazily on the first qualifying GEMM, which can be the first real request - after the giant shared KV backing buffer exists. The workspace could then land in that segment's rounding tail and pin the whole segment at engine shutdown (observed: 261 GiB retained in-process on MI350X).

Also make the shared KV backing page-padding (#53698) ROCm-only: NIXL and `SimpleCPUOffload` rely on `storage.nbytes()` matching the logical KV size, which any padding breaks (fixes #53974).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix int32 token offset overflow in fused SiLU block quant
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53390.

`silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` used a 32-bit `token_idx` when computing
global input and output row offsets. For sufficiently large token batches,
`token_idx * (2 * hidden_size)` overflowed `INT32_MAX`, wrapped the input
pointer, and caused an illegal CUDA memory access.

Widen `token_idx` to `int64_t`, matching the sibling activation kernels. This
keeps the row-offset arithmetic in 64 bits without widening unrelated
thread, group, or dimension indices.

Add a focused regression test at the first overflowing token count. The test
launches the standalone op, synchronizes to surface CUDA faults, and compares
the previously overflowing final row with the same input processed by a safe
one-token invocation.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR references #53390. A keyword search for
`silu_and_mul_per_block_quant overflow` found no open PR addressing this
integer-overflow bug. The open Triton implementation PR #39641 concerns a
different feature and does not fix this CUDA kernel's row addressing.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix] Bind RayExecutorV2 TCPStore before publishing its port
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`RayExecutorV2` initialized its torch.distributed world group in two separate steps:

```text
driver (possibly another node)                 rank-0 Ray actor
-----------------------------                  ----------------
choose/probe a free integer port
close the probing socket
publish tcp://<rank-0-ip>:<port>  -----------> init_process_group(...)
                                                TCPStore binds <port>
```

This has two independent correctness problems:

1. On a multi-node placement, the driver can probe a port on the wrong host. Port occupancy is host-local state.
2. Even if the probe is moved to the rank-0 actor, `get_open_port()` closes its socket before returning. Another process can bind the port before `init_process_group()` creates TCPStore. That is still a TOCTOU race.

The second window includes a Ray RPC back to the driver and the dispatch of every worker initialization RPC. Concurrent engine cold starts make the collision much easier to hit.

## Fix

Rank 0 now creates the actual server before publishing its address:

```text
rank-0 Ray actor                               driver / other ranks
----------------                              --------------------
TCPStore(host, port=0, is_master=True,
         wait_for_workers=False,
         multi_tenant=True)
  kernel atomically selects + binds port
  actor retains Store ownership
return tcp://<actor-ip>:<store.port>  --------> initialize workers
                                                rank 0 reuses server
                                                remote ranks connect as clients
```

`port=0` delegates selection and binding to the kernel in one operation. The actor retains the Store, so the listening socket is never released between selection and publication.

PyTorch documents `multi_tenant=True` as sharing the underlying `TCPServer` between TCPStore instances in the same process with the same host/port. Therefore the existing `tcp://` rendezvous remains unchanged: rank 0's later master TCPStore reuses the already-bound server, while nonzero ranks create clients.

There is no fallback and no application-managed port window. The change is limited to `RayExecutorV2`; legacy Ray V1 is intentionally unchanged.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- #45960 mitigated co-located DP collisions with deterministic port windows, but it still selected an unbound integer before TCPStore bind and did not make a driver-side probe valid on a remote rank-0 host. This PR replaces that window machinery for Ray V2.
- #50965 fixes reserved-range behavior inside `get_open_port()`; this PR removes `get_open_port()` from this call site.
- #50960 is already merged and removes the analogous ZMQ MessageQueue probe/bind window by binding XPUB to port 0 directly. The latest `main` containing that fix is merged into this branch.
- #51018 covers the separate DP world-group coordination port lifecycle; it does not cover this Ray V2 executor TCPStore.
- #50999 handles single-node executor rendezvous with FileStore. Ray V2 may place rank 0 on another node because it calls `initialize_ray_cluster(..., require_gpu_on_driver=False)`, so it requires a network-reachable TCPStore.
- #53666 (merged after this PR was opened) patched the driver-side `_select_tcpstore_port` so co-located non-DP replicas pick different ports, with `test_colocated_tcpstore_ports_differ`. This PR removes `_select_tcpstore_port` entirely: the port is bound with `port=0` on the rank-0 host and held in `_dist_init_store`, so distinct ports per co-located replica are guaranteed by the kernel. The merge of `main` therefore drops #53666's patch and its test deliberately — it is subsumed, not regressed.
- RFC #51275 tracks the wider port-lifecycle work. The duplicate searches for `51275 in:body` and `RayExecutorV2 TCPStore port` found no other open PR covering this Ray V2 call site.

## Tests

### Repository checks

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_ray_v2_executor.py \
  -k dist_init_store_owns_port -q

pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py \
  tests/distributed/test_ray_v2_executor.py

pre-commit run mypy-3.12 \
  --files vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py \
  --hook-stage manual
```

Results:

- Targeted pytest in a CUDA vLLM image: `1 passed, 21 deselected`.
- All changed-file pre-commit hooks passed.
- Python 3.10 and 3.12 mypy passed.
- Same-process server reuse was also checked for all `use_libuv` pairs (`True/True`, `True/False`, `False/True`, and `False/False`); all reused the held server successfully on Linux.

The unit test asserts three observable invariants:

1. the published port is nonzero;
2. a competing socket gets Linux `EADDRINUSE` while the actor holds the Store;
3. a second master TCPStore with `multi_tenant=True` can reuse the same server and exchange a key.

### Deterministic Linux A/B

This script forces the old race, validates the final handoff with a real two-process Gloo all-reduce, and stress-checks 128 concurrent ephemeral servers:

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import multiprocessing as mp
import socket
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from datetime import timedelta

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

# Old path: probe -> close -> later bind. A contender deterministically wins.
probe = socket.socket()
probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
old_port = probe.getsockname()[1]
probe.close()

contender = socket.socket()
contender.bind(("127.0.0.1", old_port))
contender.listen()
try:
    dist.TCPStore(
        "127.0.0.1", old_port, 1, True,
        wait_for_workers=False, multi_tenant=True,
    )
except Exception as exc:
    assert "EADDRINUSE" in str(exc) or "address already in use" in str(exc).lower()
    print("old: EADDRINUSE (expected)")
else:
    raise AssertionError("old path unexpectedly rebound a stolen port")
finally:
    contender.close()

# Final path: rank 0 binds port=0 and holds the Store before publication.
ctx = mp.get_context("fork")
port_q, result_q, start = ctx.Queue(), ctx.Queue(), ctx.Event()

def rank0():
    held = dist.TCPStore(
        "127.0.0.1", 0, 2, True, timedelta(seconds=15),
        wait_for_workers=False, multi_tenant=True,
    )
    port_q.put(held.port)
    start.wait()
    dist.init_process_group(
        "gloo", init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{held.port}",
        rank=0, world_size=2, timeout=timedelta(seconds=15),
    )
    value = torch.tensor([1])
    dist.all_reduce(value)
    result_q.put((0, value.item()))
    dist.destroy_process_group()

def rank1(port):
    start.wait()
    dist.init_process_group(
        "gloo", init_method=f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{port}",
        rank=1, world_size=2, timeout=timedelta(seconds=15),
    )
    value = torch.tensor([1])
    dist.all_reduce(value)
    result_q.put((1, value.item()))
    dist.destroy_process_group()

p0 = ctx.Process(target=rank0)
p0.start()
new_port = port_q.get(timeout=10)
with socket.socket() as sock:
    try:
        sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", new_port))
    except OSError as exc:
        assert exc.errno == 98
    else:
        raise AssertionError("published port was not held")

p1 = ctx.Process(target=rank1, args=(new_port,))
p1.start()
```
